title: Endpoint Privilege Manager Overview
content:
CyberArk Endpoint Privilege Manager (EPM) enforces least privilege on endpoints by controlling which applications can run with elevated privileges. EPM removes local admin rights while ensuring users can still perform their work without IT intervention.

## Key Capabilities

### Application Control

EPM uses policies to control application execution:
- Allow: Application runs normally
- Elevate: Application runs with admin privileges without requiring admin credentials
- Block: Application is prevented from running
- Restrict: Application runs with reduced privileges

### Privilege Management

- Remove local admin rights from standard users
- Elevate specific applications on-demand with justification
- Time-limited privilege elevation with automatic revocation
- Just-in-time admin access with approval workflows

### Threat Protection

- Credential theft protection (block credential harvesting tools)
- Ransomware protection (block unauthorized encryption)
- Deception-based detection with honeypot accounts

## Deployment Architecture

EPM consists of:
1. EPM Server (SaaS or on-premises)
2. EPM Agent installed on endpoints (Windows, Mac, Linux)
3. EPM Console for policy management

## Creating Policies

### Basic Application Elevation Policy

```xml
<Policy>
  <Name>Elevate-DevTools</Name>
  <Action>Elevate</Action>
  <Targets>
    <Application>
      <Publisher>Microsoft Corporation</Publisher>
      <ProductName>Visual Studio</ProductName>
    </Application>
  </Targets>
  <Conditions>
    <UserGroup>Developers</UserGroup>
    <Justification required="true" />
  </Conditions>
</Policy>
```

### Block Policy for Known Threats

To block a known malicious application:
1. Navigate to Policies > Application Control
2. Create new Block policy
3. Add file hash, publisher, or path-based criteria
4. Assign to target endpoint sets
5. Deploy policy

## EPM Agent Commands

```bash
# Check agent status
CyberArkEPMAgent.exe /status

# Force policy update
CyberArkEPMAgent.exe /update

# View agent logs
CyberArkEPMAgent.exe /logs
```

## Reporting

EPM provides built-in reports:
- Privilege elevation events by user and application
- Blocked application attempts
- Admin rights usage analysis
- Compliance dashboards for audit

## Integration with CyberArk Identity

EPM integrates with CyberArk Identity for:
- Single sign-on to the EPM Console
- MFA for privilege elevation requests
- Unified user directory and group management
- Consolidated audit logs across EPM and Identity
